Hi Vijayan

I am not sure it is the best route to start learning both GIRF and R in the same time. Maybe once you get a good understanding of GIRF and can provide a detailed list of the various steps involved in GIRF (check the draft made at the end of https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/tsdyn/XFF6lKOjqww), we can investigate how they can be implemented with package tsDyn?

Best

Matthieu

Le 29. 05. 14 00:23, Vijayan Thankappan a écrit :
Hello tsDyn users,
I know impulse response functions are not yet available in the package for threshold error correction models. But I wanted to know if anyone has tried to generate a code for TVECM IRFs for their individual use. If yes, is it possible to share the code here? Would really help me who is only starting to understand both statistical procedure of IRFs and the R language.

Sincerely,
Vijayan

parts:
Hi Vijayan

Ok, good, so first phase is done... seems to know now what should be done. But it would be good that you are sure about it, and comparing the steps from Venditi and those from Potter would be very helpful. Look anc ompare eventually the steps highlighted in the e-mail? https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/tsdyn/XFF6lKOjqww
Also, is the data from the studies you mention available? This would help benchmark your results.

So tell us which steps were you able to implement, and which ones pose problem to you? Briefly, step 1 seems trivial, step 2 requires the use of TVAR.sim() with the argument innov (  1) from sampled residuals and d, 2) from sampled residuals only ) and starting (from step 1). Step 3 seems simple too, for step 4 you might use replicate(), and for five make a loop to capture all p sequences (am I right p is the lag order?).

Try these maybe on a simple reproducible example (From ?TVAR), a simple TVAR in levels?
tv <- TVAR(data, lag=2, plot=FALSE)

and let's see which problem you encounter?

Best

Mat

It seems I am wrong in thinking that there are two ways of producing IRFs. Seems both procedures are the same. Only improvement is in handling heteroskedasticity in the second method.

Thank you,
Vijayan
